data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'gipes' meaning handsome. In the Middle Ages, a 'gibson' referred to a young knight or page. In modern times, the name has been associated with the Scottish clan Gibson, and the famous Gibson guitars. The name Gibson carries the meaning “Handsome” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Gibson usually hope their child will grow to embody handsome and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of beauty, strength, and courage.
data.etymology: Gibson belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Handsome.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gibson total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Gibson" has historical roots in Old English language and Medieval society. It originally meant 'handsome', reflecting ideas of beauty, grace, and chivalry. In later centuries, it became the surname of a prominent Scottish clan and an iconic brand of guitars, further shaping its cultural significance.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Gibson" can be interpreted as a reflection of the divine beauty and grace of God. As a derivative of 'gipes', the name invites us to see ourselves and others as created in the image of God, worthiness of honor, reverence, and love. Through its historical and contemporary associations, Gibson can also inspire us to be knights of righteousness, serving others with humility, courage, and faith.
